statements.reason: Pooled OLS arrest coefficient is -0.633 (F134, F104, F146).
Two-way FE arrest coefficient is -0.360 (F81), but it is an elasticity, not a percentage-point effect; 1% higher arrest probability goes with a 0.360% lower crime rate.
County FE arrest coefficient is -0.395 (F80, F105); -0.359 matches neither the county FE nor the two-way FE value (-0.360).
Conventional SE is 0.027 (F19) and clustered SE is 0.093 (F20), so the values are correct.
Clustering changes only the standard error (0.093, F20); the police coefficient stays 0.422 (F17, F18), as the design notes.
The Breusch-Pagan LM statistic in the table is 191.60 (F128), not 119.60.
Two-way FE police coefficient is 0.422 (F97), a positive sign, so the claim that more police reduces crime contradicts the table; it also is causal language on an associational design.
White LM = 410.04 with p < 0.0001 (F131, F133), so homoskedasticity is rejected.
The arrest coefficient -0.360 is significant (***) in the two-way FE model, but significance does not justify a causal claim on observational data with simultaneity.
N = 630 (F144) and pooled R² = 0.805 (F145) are both correct.
